_comment: The angle pool: what a carousel is ABOUT, one line each.
This file exists because the repetition problem is not that the model
forgets what it wrote. It is that the prompt is a constant. Same system
text, same three examples, same ask - so the modal answer is the same
answer, and the corpus plus the prompt between them name sleep, food,
motivation, recovery, work ethic and comparing yourself about twenty
times. Asking for variety inside that prompt does not produce variety.
Handing the model a different subject does.
So one angle is drawn per carousel, least-recently-offered first (see
state/angles-used.json), and only the drawn ones go into the prompt. The
pool can grow to any size without the brief getting one line longer.
These are TERRITORIES, not hooks. The hook formulas do not change - a
count plus a career consequence, threat or proof. The angle decides what
the five items are about underneath that hook.
House constraints every entry here already respects, so that a drawn
angle can never pull the copy off-voice:
- broad, about the player's own habits and behaviour, never the app
- never position-specific (that is the CTA slide's job, not content)
- career stakes: what is stopping you, or what the ones who make it do
- a 14-22 year old at a club or academy has actually lived it
Adding to this file is the cheapest possible way to make the account less
repetitive. Add freely. Nothing needs to change in the code.
